record.original_question: Consider the layered geodesic-net construction G_n(phi) built from seven equally spaced outer vertices, an inner seven-vertex layer determined by a deviation parameter phi, and subsequent layers V_i produced by the paper's suspension-and-winging rules. For odd i, define the suspension angle phi_i(phi) as the angle OPv between the ray from the center O of the outer circle to the relevant hook P and the segment Pv for a vertex v in V_i. For even i, define phi_i(phi) as the angle OXv, where X is the third vertex of the equilateral triangle on the relevant outer pair P,Q and v lies in V_i. Does the derivative sequence phi_i'(0) ever repeat, or is it nonrepeating for all i?

evidence.quote: Definition 4.5.1 (Suspension angle for one-hook suspensions, layers Vi for i odd). Whenever we do a one-hook suspension for a layer Vi, we are connecting a vertex v to the closest vertex on the outer circle. Denote the center of the outer circle by O and the hook by P. Then we define the suspension angle ϕi to be the angle ∠OPv.

Definition 4.5.2 (Suspension angle for two-hook suspensions, layers Vi for i even). Whenever we do a two-hook suspension for a layer Vi, we are connecting a vertex v to the closest two vertices on the outer circle P and Q through the Fermat point of ΔPvQ. As before, we denote by X the third vertex of the equilateral triangle ΔPQX used for the construction of the Fermat point. Let O be the center of the outer circle. Then we define the suspension angle ϕi to be the angle ∠OXv.
Conjecture 4.5.7. ϕ′i (0) is a sequence that never repeats itself.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a circle C of radius 1 in the Euclidean plane with center O, and place seven equally spaced "outer" vertices u_0, …, u_6 on C. For a real parameter φ in a small neighborhood of 0, build a layered planar graph G_n(φ) whose vertex set is the disjoint union of layers V_0, V_1, …, V_n as follows.

• Layer V_0 consists of the seven outer vertices u_0, …, u_6.
• Layer V_1 ("inner layer") consists of seven vertices, each obtained from a corresponding outer vertex by rotating about O by an angle φ and scaling radially; the parameter φ measures the angular deviation of the inner heptagon from being concentrically aligned with V_0.
• For i ≥ 2 the layer V_i is produced from V_{i−1} by the following alternating "suspension-and-winging" rule:
   – If i is odd, perform a one-hook suspension: each new vertex v ∈ V_i is connected to its closest vertex P on the outer circle (the "hook"), forming an edge Pv.
   – If i is even, perform a two-hook suspension: each new vertex v ∈ V_i is connected through the Fermat point of the triangle ΔPvQ to its two closest outer vertices P and Q; let X denote the third vertex of the equilateral triangle erected on PQ (on the side away from v) used in the standard Fermat-point construction.

Define the suspension angle φ_i(φ) by
   φ_i(φ) = ∠OPv,   if i is odd (with P the hook used in layer V_i and v ∈ V_i),
   φ_i(φ) = ∠OXv,   if i is even (with X the auxiliary equilateral-triangle vertex described above and v ∈ V_i).

Each φ_i(φ) is a smooth function of φ near φ = 0. Consider the sequence of derivatives
   a_i := φ_i'(0),   i = 1, 2, 3, … .

Question: Is the sequence (a_i)_{i ≥ 1} nonrepeating, in the sense that a_i ≠ a_j whenever i ≠ j? Equivalently, prove or disprove that no two terms of the derivative sequence (φ_i'(0)) coincide.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is stated as a conjecture in the source on geodesic nets and open problems. A web search did not surface any subsequent work resolving it; related follow-up work on geodesic nets (e.g., recent papers on stationary geodesic nets and constructions with few boundary vertices) does not address this specific derivative-sequence conjecture, so it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Paper presenting geodesic-net constructions and a list of open problems including the suspension-angle derivative conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture that φ_i'(0) is a nonrepeating sequence is stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Towards Constructing Geodesic Nets with Four Boundary Vertices and an Increasing Number of Balanced Vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Recent follow-up work on geodesic-net constructions; does not resolve the suspension-angle derivative conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of this conjecture appears in subsequent geodesic-net literature found via search.
